requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
a readable statement when successfully read and parsed current source contains
no citations within the scope of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`.

Missing, unreadable, or unparseable current source MUST instead produce a
visible diagnostic, without preventing the rest of the book from rendering.
These failures MUST NOT be presented as an absence of coverage explanations.
rationale:
The tests adequately cover `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.availability`.

Obligations derived from the text:
1. Source that is read and parsed successfully and has no in-scope citations MUST show a readable statement.
2. Missing, unreadable or unparseable source MUST produce a visible diagnostic, and the rest of the book MUST still render.
3. Those failures MUST NOT be presented as an absence of coverage explanations.

Mapping to tests in `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs`:
- **Clean source with no citations.**
  - `mod[tests]/fn[absent_citations_are_distinct_from_missing_unreadable_and_unparseable_source]` renders `fn ordinary() {}`. It asserts the "No coverage explanations are present" statement and asserts there is no "Coverage notes unavailable" text.
  - `mod[tests]/fn[citations_on_modules_and_citation_text_in_literals_do_not_create_explanations]` renders source with a module-level citation, a nested module and citation text inside a string literal. All of these are out of scope, so it asserts the "none present" statement and asserts that no "exception proposal" and no "Module only." text appears.
- **Unparseable source.** The first test writes two different syntactically invalid sources. Each must contain "Coverage notes unavailable" and "syntax error", and must not contain the "No coverage explanations" statement.
- **Missing source.** The test removes `code.rs`. It asserts the diagnostic is shown and the "none present" statement is not.
- **Unreadable source.** The test makes `code.rs` a directory. It asserts the diagnostic is shown and the "none present" statement is not.
- **Failure does not block rendering.** The test calls `pages` with two files, `code.rs` and `missing.rs`. Both fail, and it asserts that two chapters are still produced and that each carries the diagnostic. The failure of the first file therefore does not abort the rest. The test never pairs a failing file with a good one, but `pages` maps files independently and returns one chapter per file, so this is not a meaningful gap.
- **Not presented as absence.** Every failure case asserts that the "No coverage explanations are present" statement is absent.

The helpers `fixture` and `render` are reached from the marked tests. `render` also checks the chapter count and path. The assertions match the requirement, and I found no plausible violating behavior that these tests would accept. I read only the implementation code needed to check these assertions, and I did not judge its correctness.

The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments

{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.

function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
